haiku-low.q1: When the caller's transaction commits; enqueue inserts a pending row inside it. The row exists only if that transaction commits.
haiku-low.q2: It is redelivered after 30 seconds, possibly to a different consumer. How long the broker keeps an unacknowledged message is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: 5 attempts, waiting 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2 to 5. After attempt 5 fails, the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset, each after 3+ days on the service. Last move needs order_confirmed p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay under 60 seconds.
haiku-low.q5: The notification id, sent as idempotency_key. If MailRelay accepted that key within 24 hours, it drops the repeat send and reports success.
haiku-low.q6: The outbox relay publishes it to notifications.requested, then sets published_at after broker confirms. Doc does not explicitly define when the monolith is done.
haiku-low.q7: The row's route, set at enqueue from notify.route.<type>. It is decided at enqueue; if the flag cannot be read, the route is monolith.
haiku-low.q8: The deliveries table: an existing notification id skips the insert. The MailRelay idempotency key (notification id) also blocks a repeat send.
haiku-low.q9: After storing the row, before sending. Crash before ack: redelivery is a no-op. Crash after MailRelay accepts: resent with same key.
haiku-low.q10: In the service's deliveries table, as attempts and next_attempt_at. The service's sender loop picks due pending rows and acts on them.
haiku-low.q11: They stay on the service: the relay keeps publishing them and the service finishes them. Nothing is re-sent.
haiku-low.q12: Per message: notification id, type, user email, payload and creation time. The service renders the email content from its own template copies.

sonnet.q1: It becomes durable when the monolith's `enqueue_notification` inserts a `pending` row inside the caller's transaction and that transaction commits. Whether the caller's transaction commits decides if it exists; on rollback there is no row and no message.
sonnet.q2: The broker redelivers it after 30 seconds, possibly to a different consumer (at-least-once).
sonnet.q3: Up to 5 attempts, with waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2, 3, 4 and 5. A timeout counts as a failure. If attempt 5 fails, the row is set to `failed` and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: Order: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset. Each runs on the service at least 3 days before the next moves. Before password_reset moves, order_confirmed must have run on the service at least 3 days and the service must have shown p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency under 60 seconds on order_confirmed (measured from the message creation time to `accepted_at`).
sonnet.q5: The idempotency key. It is the notification id, on both the monolith and service sides. If MailRelay already accepted a send with the same key in the last 24 hours, it drops the new send and reports success.
sonnet.q6: The row is enqueued with route `service`. The outbox relay polls for `service` rows with no `published_at` and publishes a message to topic `notifications.requested`. The service consumer picks it up. The monolith's part is done when the broker confirms the message and the relay sets `published_at`.
sonnet.q7: The `route` field on the row, set by `enqueue_notification` from the flag `notify.route.<type>` at enqueue time. It defaults to `monolith` if the flag cannot be read. It is fixed at enqueue.
sonnet.q8: The consumer inserts into `deliveries` keyed by notification id. If the id already exists it skips the insert, so no second row is created and no second send happens. The MailRelay idempotency key is a further backstop.
sonnet.q9: It acknowledges only after the `deliveries` row is stored, which is before sending (the sender loop sends later). If it crashes before acknowledging, the broker redelivers after 30 seconds and the stored row makes it a no-op. If it crashes after MailRelay accepts but before recording `sent`, the row is still `pending`, so it is re-sent with the same key and MailRelay drops the repeat.
sonnet.q10: In the service's `deliveries` table, in the `attempts` and `next_attempt_at` fields. The service's sender loop acts on it, picking `pending` rows that are due.
sonnet.q11: They stay routed to the service. The relay keeps publishing them and the service finishes them. Only new rows get the monolith route. Nothing is re-sent because each row still has one owner.
sonnet.q12: Each message carries the notification id, type, user email, payload and creation time. The email content is rendered in the service by the sender loop, using the service's own copies of the templates.
